intro.title: Toggle Visibility
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React component that can show and hide content by clicking a button. You'll learn how to use React's useState hook to manage a boolean state value that controls whether content is visible or hidden. The core programming concept is conditional rendering, where you display different JSX elements based on the current state value. You'll work with React hooks, event handlers, and JavaScript's logical operators to create an interactive toggle functionality. By the end of this lesson, you'll understand how to control what users see on screen based on user interactions and component state.
intro.usecase: Toggle visibility is one of the most common interaction patterns in web applications, powering everything from dropdown menus and collapsible sidebars to modal dialogs and expandable content sections. You'll find it in dashboard panels that can be minimized to save space, FAQ sections where answers expand when clicked, mobile navigation menus that slide in and out, and form sections that reveal additional fields based on user selections. This pattern is essential for creating clean, user-friendly interfaces that don't overwhelm users with information, allowing them to control what content they see and when they see it. Modern applications like Slack's channel lists, GitHub's file explorers, and e-commerce filter panels all rely heavily on toggle visibility to manage complex information hierarchies.
